2026-12-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Do not turn away from the living God
Your eye is the lamp of your body
2026-12-12.verse: Your eye is the lamp of your body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light.
theo: Hebrews warns: “Take care… that none of you may have an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called ‘today’.” The generation in the desert did not enter God's rest because of unbelief. Today is always the day to listen.

Jesus speaks of the eye as the lamp of the body: what we look at shapes what we become. “Consider whether the light in you is not darkness.” In the weeks before Christmas, guarding our eyes and hearts makes room for the true Light who is coming into the world.

2026-12-12.prayer: Lord, light of the world, keep my heart soft to your voice today, and fill my eyes and my whole being with your light. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the veil is opened and our eyes are turned to the altar. What we contemplate there fills the whole body with light.

quick: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your heart.

2026-12-12.action: Encourage a friend in faith today.
2026-12-12.question: What am I letting into my eyes and heart?

family.explain: Jesus says our eyes are like a lamp. When we look at good things, our hearts are full of light.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that we may use our phones and screens wisely.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we spend less time on screens and more time together this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, fill our eyes and hearts with your light. As we gather today, soften our hearts and teach us to encourage one another. Amen.
share: Hebrews warns against a hardened heart (Hebrews 3:12). Where has my heart grown cold?
What do my eyes look at most each day, and does it bring light or darkness?
Whom will I encourage in faith this week?
pm.resp: Lord, fill us with your light.
interc: For the Church, that her members may encourage one another daily in faith.
For those who have drifted away from God, that their hearts may be softened.
For young people addicted to screens and impure images, that they may be set free.
For families, that they may spend time together in love and prayer.
For our prayer group, that we may be a support to one another.
pm.close: Lord God, you speak to us today. Keep our hearts from hardening, guard the lamp of our eyes, and make us a community that encourages one another until your Son comes. Amen.

illus: A grandmother in Changanacherry noticed her grandson spending every evening on his phone in his room. Instead of scolding, she asked him to help her read the Bible because her eyes were weak. Slowly the evenings changed. Encouragement worked where criticism had failed.

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews gives a warning: take care, brothers and sisters, that none of you may have an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God (Hebrews 3:12). Faith is not lost in one day. It drifts away little by little when the heart grows hard.
The writer remembers the generation in the desert: they saw God's wonders, yet they grumbled and did not trust, and so they did not enter the promised rest. Faith must be renewed day by day.

Then he gives the remedy: exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin (Hebrews 3:13). We need one another. A Christian alone easily grows cold, like a coal taken out of the fire.

In the Gospel Jesus says: your eye is the lamp of your body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light; but if it is not healthy, your body is full of darkness (Luke 11:34). What we look at shapes who we become.
Our eyes today are flooded with images: violence, impurity, luxury, envy. Hours on the screen can fill the soul with darkness without our noticing. Jesus asks us to guard the lamp of the eye.
This Nombu, consider a fast of the eyes: less time on the phone, no impure images, more time looking at the Gospel, at the faces of our families, at the beauty of creation, at the crib.
And let us encourage one another. Send a word of faith to a friend who has drifted. Invite someone to the Holy Qurbana. Today, while it is called today, let us not harden our hearts. Amen.
kids: Children, your eyes are like windows. Let good things come in through them, and your heart will be full of light!

As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”
points.apply: Listen to God in five minutes of silence today.

q: Two are better than one… For if they fall, one will lift up the other.
